proposal.description_long: On Jan. 14, 2019, The Atlantic published “Trump 50,” a retrospective examining 50 incidents from Donald Trump’s presidency. The magazine described the project as an analysis of events it considered improbable, norm-bending and destructive. Editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg said the list was not intended as a partisan exercise and explained that the magazine selected incidents it could not imagine occurring in most other presidencies. These are the publication’s descriptions and editorial judgments, not an independent measurement of institutional change. The available evidence establishes that The Atlantic compiled and presented a retrospective. It does not show that this package caused new guardrails, changed government policy, or measurably reinforced a particular guardrail argument. This version narrows the record to the documented publication and its stated framing. Any claim about subsequent consequences would require separate evidence identifying the safeguard, decision-maker and resulting change.

proposal.description_long: On Aug. 9, 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told his cabinet that Israel did not accept the 15-point Gaza document and that Israeli forces would not withdraw until Hamas was disarmed. Reuters reported his remarks and described the document as Donald Trump’s latest Gaza plan. The Associated Press later reported that Netanyahu rejected Trump’s plan to advance the stalled Gaza ceasefire and conditioned Israeli withdrawal from territory under Israeli control on complete Hamas disarmament. These reports support a public disagreement over the terms and sequencing of a Gaza plan. They do not support the original record’s allegation that Trump signed an “Islamabad Memorandum” with Iran or that Israeli officials warned a separate conflict would resume within days. This proposal replaces that unsupported subject with the different Gaza event documented by the supplied AP URL and Reuters. It makes no claim that the plan was accepted, a withdrawal occurred, or Hamas disarmed.
